# AMD Instinct validation campaign for vLLM ROCm serving parity

## Description

This epic delivers the go/no-go decision data for AMD GPU enablement: a
validation campaign run on dedicated physical AMD Instinct nodes that
establishes functional and performance parity data for vLLM serving of the
platform's supported model set on ROCm, and produces the recommended
productization scope — the list of models that clear. The platform ships
only CUDA runtime builds today and has no first-hand parity data for ROCm;
this campaign is the strategy's P0 prerequisite for productizing a supported
vLLM ROCm serving runtime.

## Scope

- Secure access to dedicated AMD Instinct nodes for the campaign — via
  procurement or a partner-lab arrangement (currently unresolved; an
  external dependency with uncertain timing tracked as a risk on this epic).
- Stand up the node software stack needed to run the campaign on those
  nodes: the ROCm driver and the accelerator discovery stack that exposes
  `amd.com/gpu` resources to the cluster.
- Define the validation matrix: the supported model set to be covered, the
  functional pass/fail criteria per model, and the performance comparison
  baseline (the productized CUDA vLLM runtime serving the same models).
- Deploy upstream/community vLLM ROCm builds through the platform serving
  path — KServe InferenceServices backed by a serving runtime — on the AMD
  Instinct nodes, since no productized ROCm runtime exists yet.
- Execute the campaign: per-model functional validation (serving
  correctness) and per-model performance measurement (throughput and
  latency) against the defined baseline.
- Produce the validation report: per-model functional and performance
  results, parity assessment, and the recommended go/no-go scope for
  productization (the cleared model list), with environment details
  (hardware model, driver and ROCm versions) recorded for reproducibility.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Dedicated AMD Instinct node access is secured and the nodes run campaign
  workloads: the driver and accelerator discovery stack are functional and
  `amd.com/gpu` resources are schedulable on the validation nodes.
- Every model in the supported model set has a recorded functional pass/fail
  result for vLLM ROCm serving through the platform serving path (KServe
  InferenceServices).
- Every model in the supported model set has recorded performance
  measurements (throughput and latency) against the defined comparison
  baseline.
- The validation report states, per model, whether it meets the functional
  and performance parity criteria, and gives a recommended go/no-go scope
  for productization (the cleared model list).
- The report records the environment (hardware model, driver and ROCm
  versions) and any deviations, so results are reproducible.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): A validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware
  establishes functional and performance parity data for vLLM serving of
  the supported model set, producing the go/no-go scope for productization —
  covered in full by this epic.

# Productize the supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime

## Description

This epic delivers the supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime for the models
the AMD Instinct validation campaign clears: a productized ROCm build of the
vLLM serving runtime image from the existing midstream vLLM repository, its
supported runtime definition for AMD GPU nodes, and the build/release
integration for the new image variant. Today the component productizes only
CUDA (NVIDIA) builds; ROCm builds exist upstream but are not shipped or
supported.

## Scope

- Build the ROCm variant of the vLLM serving runtime image in the existing
  midstream vLLM repository, based on AMD's published ROCm runtime images.
- Add the ROCm image variant to the component's existing build-and-release
  pipeline (the component is already onboarded; this is a new variant in the
  same pipeline, not a new repository or component).
- Define the supported runtime for AMD GPU nodes — a ServingRuntime that
  deploys the ROCm image and requests `amd.com/gpu` resources — covering the
  model list cleared by the validation campaign.
- Pin and document the ROCm base image version used, with an assessment of
  how AMD's ROCm image release cadence aligns with the platform release
  trains (an external dependency outside our control, flagged as a strategy
  open question).
- Extend license-scan coverage to the new ROCm transitive dependency stack
  introduced by the image variant.
- Validate the serving path on AMD Instinct nodes: KServe InferenceServices
  scheduling and serving through the new runtime. KServe itself requires no
  code changes for this and is validated here as a keep-working component.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The ROCm vLLM runtime image builds green through the component's build
  pipeline and is released as a supported artifact for the platform version.
- A supported runtime definition exists that deploys the ROCm image on AMD
  GPU nodes (`amd.com/gpu`) and serves every model on the list cleared by
  the validation campaign.
- Functional and performance results for the cleared models meet the parity
  thresholds established by the validation campaign when served by the
  productized runtime.
- KServe InferenceServices using the ROCm serving runtime schedule onto AMD
  Instinct nodes and serve inference successfully (passive-component
  validation for KServe).
- Existing CUDA-based serving runtimes and NVIDIA-hosted inference
  workloads continue to work unchanged (non-regression; the ROCm runtime is
  additive).
- The license scan of the ROCm dependency stack completes with no
  unresolved prohibitive findings.
- The ROCm base image version is pinned, and its cadence alignment with
  platform release trains is documented.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): A supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime is productized for the
  models the validation campaign clears — covered in full by this epic,
  including the KServe passive-component validation.

# PyTorch ROCm training support in the Training Operator

## Description

This epic delivers ROCm support for PyTorch training jobs: single- and
multi-GPU PyTorchJobs executing ROCm-based training on AMD Instinct nodes,
mirroring the platform's existing CUDA training support path. Together with
the Kueue quota-handling work in the Distributed Workloads component, it
fulfils the strategy's training requirement.

## Scope

- Enable PyTorchJob workloads to run ROCm-based PyTorch training on AMD GPU
  nodes for single-GPU and multi-GPU job topologies, mirroring the existing
  CUDA support path.
- Provide the supported PyTorch ROCm execution path for training jobs, based
  on upstream PyTorch ROCm builds.
- Schedule training worker pods onto AMD GPU nodes (`amd.com/gpu`
  resources), with correct GPU visibility and assignment across workers in
  multi-GPU jobs.
- Validate end to end, jointly with Kueue admission of the jobs, on physical
  AMD Instinct hardware (hardware access shared with the serving validation
  campaign as a coordination point — noted as a risk, not a blocker for
  starting the code work).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A single-GPU PyTorchJob runs ROCm training to completion on an AMD
  Instinct node.
- A multi-GPU PyTorchJob runs distributed ROCm training across multiple AMD
  GPUs, admitted through Kueue with all-or-nothing (gang) semantics.
- Training worker pods requesting `amd.com/gpu` are placed on AMD GPU nodes
  and execute with correct GPU visibility/assignment across workers.
- Existing CUDA-based PyTorchJob behavior is unchanged (non-regression).
- Validation executed on physical AMD Instinct nodes is recorded (with
  resource-level validation on substitute resource names acceptable as an
  interim state before hardware access is secured).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for single- and
  multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling —
  this epic covers the PyTorchJob execution half (job runs ROCm training on
  AMD GPUs); the Kueue admission and quota half is covered by the
  Distributed Workloads quota-handling epic.

# Kueue amd.com/gpu quota handling for ROCm workloads

## Description

This epic delivers `amd.com/gpu` quota handling in the Distributed Workloads
stack: Kueue admission of single- and multi-GPU ROCm jobs with AMD GPU quota
accounting, so that PyTorch training jobs requesting AMD GPUs are queued,
admitted, and quota-enforced the same way NVIDIA GPU workloads are today.

## Scope

- Support `amd.com/gpu` as a quota-bearing resource in the Kueue queueing
  model: ClusterQueue/LocalQueue quota and resource flavors for AMD GPUs.
- Admit multi-GPU ROCm training jobs with all-or-nothing (gang) semantics
  counting `amd.com/gpu` devices.
- Enforce quota and queueing behavior for workloads requesting
  `amd.com/gpu`: pending when quota is exhausted, admitted when it frees up.
- Validate end to end, jointly with PyTorchJob training workloads requesting
  `amd.com/gpu`, on AMD Instinct nodes where hardware is available; quota
  semantics are resource-name-generic and can be validated with equivalent
  resource configuration before hardware access is secured.

## Acceptance Criteria

- ClusterQueue/LocalQueue configuration carries `amd.com/gpu` quota, and
  workloads requesting `amd.com/gpu` are admitted against that quota.
- A multi-GPU workload requesting N × `amd.com/gpu` is admitted with
  all-or-nothing semantics (no partial admission).
- Workloads requesting `amd.com/gpu` in excess of available quota remain
  pending and are admitted when quota frees up.
- Existing `nvidia.com/gpu` quota handling and queueing behavior is
  unchanged (non-regression).
- Validation on AMD Instinct nodes is recorded (or on equivalent resource
  configuration as an interim state before hardware access is secured).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for single- and
  multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling —
  this epic covers the Kueue admission and quota half; the PyTorchJob
  execution half is covered by the Training Operator ROCm enablement epic.
